title: A library reservation
premises: Every registered student may borrow books.
Anyone who may borrow books may reserve a book.
Ada is a registered student.
explanation: The rules form a chain: Ada may borrow books, so she may reserve one. With all three premises true, the conclusion cannot be false.

title: Choosing a battery
premises: Of the 100 batteries in a box, 98 can power a sensor for an hour.
One battery is selected at random, with each battery equally likely to be chosen.
conclusion: The selected battery can power the sensor for an hour.
explanation: The chance of selecting a suitable battery is 98 out of 100. That is strong support, but either of the two unsuitable batteries could still be selected.

title: An open gate
premises: If a valid ticket is scanned, the gate opens.
An attendant has now opened the gate for everyone, regardless of their tickets.
The gate opens for Bob.
explanation: The gate now opens for people with invalid tickets too. Its opening supplies no evidence about Bob's ticket. The conditional does not say that a valid ticket is the only way to open the gate.

title: Finding the rover
premises: The rover is in either the east corridor or the west corridor.
It is not in the east corridor.
conclusion: It is in the west corridor.
explanation: The first premise gives the alternatives and the second rules one out. If both premises are true, the rover must be in the west corridor.

title: A new image
premises: A classifier labels 96% of images correctly in a specified collection.
An image is selected uniformly at random from that collection.
conclusion: The classifier labels the selected image correctly.
explanation: The selection gives a 96% chance of a correct label. This supports expecting a correct result, but the selected image could belong to the remaining 4%. The stated selection matters: a deliberately chosen difficult image would be a different case.

title: The dashboard's colour
premises: The dashboard's background is blue because its designer likes blue.
The background stays blue in every kind of weather.
explanation: The background colour supplies no weather information. These premises give no reason to expect rain, even though rain remains possible.

title: No alert
premises: Whenever the detector finds an error, it sends an alert.
It sent no alert during this run.
conclusion: The detector found no error during this run.
explanation: Finding an error would have produced an alert, so the two premises rule out finding one. Notice the wording: the conclusion is not that the run contained no errors. The detector might have missed one.

title: Planning a picnic
premises: A weather forecast assigns a 90% probability to rain tomorrow.
Assume this probability correctly describes the uncertainty about tomorrow's weather.
explanation: A 90% probability is a good reason to expect rain, not a guarantee. A dry day is still compatible with the premises.

title: Reporting a trial
premises: The assistant answered 80 of 100 trial questions correctly.
It answered the other 20 incorrectly.
conclusion: The assistant answered every trial question correctly.
explanation: The premises actually contradict the conclusion: they explicitly report 20 incorrect answers. A high success rate is not the same as success on every question.

title: A necessary condition
premises: Only registered participants entered the workshop.
Mina entered the workshop.
explanation: The word 'only' makes registration necessary for entering. Since Mina entered, the general premise applies to her.

title: Drawing a counter
premises: A bag contains eight red counters and two blue counters.
One counter is drawn at random, with each counter equally likely to be drawn.
explanation: Eight of the ten equally likely outcomes are red. This makes red more likely than blue, but a blue draw is still possible.

title: A status light
premises: If the connection works, the status light is green.
The connection does not work.
conclusion: The status light is not green.
explanation: The rule describes what happens when the connection works. It gives no rule for a broken connection. The light might remain green because it is stuck, so the conclusion needs further information.
